deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the opening sheet (fol. 25r) of a Dedekind outline headed 'Galois'. It is a programme of theorems with proof sketches, not a worked computation.

LEFT COLUMN, §I.
Setup. Let f(x) be a polynomial of degree m with distinct roots x_1,…,x_m. Let S be any 'rationales Gebiet' (a field) containing its coefficients.

Hauptsatz. There is a group G of permutations of the roots (the Galois group of f over S) with two properties:
- A rational function φ(x_1,…,x_m) with coefficients in S whose value is unchanged by every σ in G has its value in S.
- Conversely, if the value of φ lies in S, then φ is unchanged by every σ in G.

Sketch of the proof.
(a) Choose a Galois resolvent v = V(x_1,…,x_m), e.g. a linear form Σ c_i x_i with c_i in S. It must take Π(m) = m! distinct values under the m! permutations. Π(m) is Gauss's notation for m!.
(b) Every rational function of the roots, in particular every x_i, is a rational function of v over S. Dedekind adds that the representation can be chosen so that applying an arbitrary permutation to both sides keeps it valid.
(c) Let R(u) = ∏_σ (u − σv), of degree m!, with coefficients in S. It splits over S into m!/g irreducible factors, all of degree g. Dedekind's reason: each value σv is rational in any other value τv. Hence all the σv generate the same field, so their minimal polynomials all have the same degree.
(d) Fix one irreducible factor F(u), with v as a root. The permutations σ that carry v to the roots of F form a group G of order g.
(e) The Hauptsatz then follows 'unmittelbar'. Implicit step (mine): write φ = R_φ(v). If φ is G-invariant, then φ equals the average (1/g) Σ_{σ∈G} R_φ(σv). This is a symmetric function of the roots of F, so it lies in S. Conversely, if φ = c with c in S, then R_φ(u) − c vanishes at v. So F divides its numerator, hence R_φ(σv) = c for all σ in G.

Further claim. G is completely characteristic of the equation f. In particular its orbits on {x_i} give the irreducible factors of f over S.

RIGHT COLUMN, fol. 25.
Setup. Let F(u) = 0 be the irreducible equation over S of degree g satisfied by v. Write its roots as ψ(v), i.e. rational functions ψ_1(v)=v, …, ψ_g(v). Composition of the ψ corresponds to the group G.

Claim 1. Let f(v) be any S-rational function of v. (The letter f is reused here; it is not the polynomial of §I.) Then f(v) satisfies an irreducible equation of degree h with g = hk. The g values f(ψ_i(v)) coincide in groups of k. Dedekind calls this 'bekanntlich' (well known). It is the standard result that conjugates come with equal multiplicity.

Claim 2. Let χ(v) range over the k functions ψ(v) with f(χ(v)) = f(v). Then these k substitutions form a group, a 'Divisor' (subgroup) of G.

Proof as written. Suppose f(χ'(v)) = f(χ''(v)) = f(v). Then f(χ'(χ''(v))) = f(χ''(v)) = f(v), so χ'(χ''(v)) is again some χ(v).

Implicit step (mine). f(χ'(u)) − f(u) is a rational function over S that vanishes at u = v. Therefore it vanishes at every root of the irreducible F, in particular at u = χ''(v). This gives f(χ'(χ''(v))) = f(χ''(v)).

Closure under composition in a finite set of substitutions of the roots of F suffices for a group. This is the stabilizer of f(v) in G. Its index h is the degree of f(v) over S, i.e. the number of distinct conjugates.

Crossed-out passage. A first attempt at the same argument (the k values χ are among the ψ; if χ′, χ″ are χ's then χ′(χ″(v)) is a χ). It was rewritten as the uncrossed text below it.

Role on the page. These are the first steps of the Galois correspondence: intermediate quantities f(v) correspond to subgroups of G, with degree = index. The next page goes on to reduce G by adjunction.
errors: No mathematical errors. The step f(χ'(χ''(v))) = f(χ''(v)) is stated without justification. It requires substituting the root χ''(v) for v in the S-rational identity f(χ'(v)) = f(v), which is valid because F is irreducible.
Notational clash: f denotes the polynomial f(x) in §I and an arbitrary rational function f(v) on the right column.
In §I the claim that all irreducible factors of the resolvent have the same degree g is justified only by mutual rational expressibility of the values of v. This is correct but terse.
Existence of a resolvent v with m! distinct values is assumed. It needs S infinite or large enough, which is fine in characteristic 0, the implicit setting.

results.what: Fundamental theorem: a rational function of the roots has its value in S iff it is invariant under the Galois group
results.modern_name: Characterization of the Galois group / fixed field of Gal(K/S) is S

results.what: Galois resolvent v with m! distinct values; all roots are rational in v; the resolvent splits into irreducible factors of equal degree g; the group is the set of permutations sending v to its conjugates
results.modern_name: Primitive element theorem / Galois resolvent construction
results.usually_credited_to: Galois (1830); Lagrange for the resolvent idea

results.what: Orbits of the group on the roots give the irreducible factors of f over S
The substitutions χ fixing f(v) form a subgroup of G whose index h is the degree of f(v) over S (g = hk)
results.usually_credited_to: Galois; systematized by Jordan (1870) and in Dedekind's Göttingen Galois lectures (1856–58)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard outline of Galois theory in Dedekind's known style: 'Gebiet' for field, 'Divisor' for subgroup, Π(m) for m!. It closely parallels his Göttingen lectures of 1856–58, which are documented and published (Scharlau 1981) and known as the first university lectures on Galois theory. Nothing here goes beyond what is already attributed to him.

checkable.asserts: For x^3-2 over Q a Galois resolvent v=x1+2x2+3x3 has irreducible degree g=6=3!, so the resolvent does not split and the group is S3.
For x^3-3x+1 (roots 2cos(2pi/9), 2cos(4pi/9), 2cos(8pi/9)) the resolvent of degree 6 splits into 6/g = 2 irreducible factors of degree g=3, so the group is cyclic of order 3.
The three listed numbers are indeed the roots of x^3-3x+1, as used in the previous check.
For the S3 case, f(v)=x1 has h=3 conjugates with stabilizer of order k=2, and f(v)=sqrt(-3) has h=2 with k=3; in both cases g = h*k = 6.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: the insertion above 'Gleichung' is 'f(x)' and the one above 'mit' is 'm'. The intended reading is 'einer Gleichung f(x) [vom Grade] m mit ungleichen Wurzeln'.

'Die Substitutionen, durch welche aus einer Wurzel eines solchen Factors alle abgeleitet werden': 'aus' and 'alle' are interlinear insertions. The machine transcription's duplicated 'abgeleitet' (once struck, once kept) appears spurious.
In the crossed-out passage the interlinear 'k' does not belong; it is inserted above 'sämmtlichen' in the following uncrossed sentence: 'Seien χ(v) die sämmtlichen k Werthe von ψ(v)'.

Crossed-out passage reads approximately: 'Sind nun χ(v) die sämmtlichen Wurzeln von F(u), f(χ(v)) die entsprechenden Werthe von f(v), so sind die χ in den ψ enthalten. Und wenn χ'(v), χ''(v) zwei χ sind, so ist auch χ'(χ''(v)) ein χ.'
'vom Grade' is an interlinear insertion before 'g' in 'irreductibele Gleichung vom Grade g'.
'f(x)' before 'vollständig charakteristisch' is an interlinear insertion: 'für die Gleichung f(x) vollständig charakteristisch'.
